newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-12 hurt as Singapore Air jet hits turbulence.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-12 hurt as Singapore Air jet hits turbulence.

text.p: Twelve people were injured when a Singapore Airlines A340 Airbus flying from Singapore to Sydney hit turbulence over Australia on Thursday night.
The plane hit an air pocket while flying over Uluru (Ayers Rock) in central Australia, causing the plane to drop 100 metres, Federal Airports Corp spokeswoman Annie Luczka said.
Singapore Airlines said nine passengers, including one pregnant woman, and three crew suffered various neck and back injuries. All were in the back of the plane.
The injured passengers and crew, who were not wearing seatbelts at the time, were escorted from the aircraft at Sydney by ambulance officers and taken to hospital.
All but one of those injured had been or would be released from hospital by Friday morning, Singapore Airlines' Australian senior marketing manager Derek Mellor told Reuters.
The one passenger remaining in hospital had had surgery for for hip injuries, he said. There were 236 passengers and 16 crew were aboard the flight SQ219.
